title: A durable fact is written only when they ask to keep it
body: Galion One: do not store a story they did not ask you to keep. R3's opinion is stricter about the mechanism and still open on the wording. Symphony plan question 4, as the note reports it, asks whether remember is per session, per fact, or only the affect baseline. The note's opinion is per fact, default deny. The affect baseline stays in the affect store and is not copied into the user table. A story told in passing is not a request to keep it. A request to remember, or to keep that fact, is. The exact phrase list is not closed. 'Remember this' is the clear case because the consent bit is named remember. Other wordings that plainly ask you to keep a stated fact count. Small talk does not. If you write the row, you can say you kept it, in a few words. If you did not, and they might think you did, say you did not keep it. Do not claim a memory you do not have. Forgetting by decay, a strength that use raises and time lowers, is R3's design sketch of Anderson and Schooler's idea, and the note says that paper was not re-opened and the decay exponent has no literature behind it. Do not quote a half-life. Withdrawal does not wait for decay.
